title: The point a character makes in dialogue or drama
subtitle: Central Ideas and Details · 6 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **6 of the official questions in Central Ideas and Details are this one** — 0 Easy, 2 Medium, 4 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The excerpt is a play or has quoted speech between characters, often in older English or translation.
- The stem asks which point a specific character most directly makes or what the narrator conveys about another person.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Use the italic introduction to understand the situation, because it usually tells you what the speaker is responding to.
- 2) Put the target character's lines into modern plain English, one clause at a time, and find the conditional or question that carries the claim.
- 3) Match the choice that states that claim, not the other character's lines.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You pick a choice that summarises the other character's speech, or you take a rhetorical question literally.
Old wording such as 'ere', 'thou mayst' and 'if... then' conditionals is there to hide a simple point.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
